title: These stories are told to you exactly as they happened.
subtitle: The Musa story ends, the lesson turns to you
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: We told you the story of Musa {idea}just as it actually happened, without increase or decrease{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says no Prophet was given a Book {reward}more complete, with more news of what has passed and what will be{/reward}.
now: You just read about a tyrant, a calf, a brother pulled by the beard. It is easy to close the app and move on. {idea}The story was told so you would see yourself in it.{/idea} Which character were you this week?
old: Quran stories are history lessons about other people.
new: They are told exactly, so I can find my own life inside them.
try: Pick one person from the Musa story who is most like you this week, and think why.

title: Turning away from the Reminder becomes a heavy load.
subtitle: What you walk away from, you carry
then: Ibn Kathir explains turning away means {trap}denying it and not following its commands, while seeking guidance from other than it{/trap}. The burden here means sin. The Quran is {idea}a final warning for everyone it reaches{/idea}.
now: You have the Quran on your phone, on the shelf, in your ears at the masjid. It has reached you. {idea}Leaving it closed is not neutral{/idea}. The kind answer is to let it in, a little at a time.
old: If I simply ignore it, I am not doing anything wrong.
new: Once it has reached me, ignoring it is a choice with weight.
try: Read one page of Quran today with its meaning, even if you only manage one.

title: An evil load to carry, with no setting it down.
subtitle: The weight that cannot be shrugged off
then: Ibn Kathir says those who turn away {trap}will not be able to avoid or escape{/trap} this burden, and it will be an evil load on the Day of Resurrection. The warning is given now, {idea}while there is still time to turn{/idea}.
now: You keep carrying a grudge, a lie, a habit, telling yourself you will deal with it later. It gets heavier. {idea}The best time to put a burden down is now{/idea}, while your hands are still free.
old: I can carry this for now and sort it out later.
new: Burdens grow. The time to put them down is while I still can.
try: Name one wrong you have been carrying and take one step today to put it down.

title: The Horn is blown, and the guilty gather in terror.
subtitle: The moment the world ends
then: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the Sur and said {idea}it is a horn that will be blown{/idea}. He said the one holding it is waiting for permission. When the Companions asked what to say, he told them: {reward}Allah is sufficient for us, and the best Protector; upon Allah we rely{/reward}.
now: You read about the end of the world and your chest tightens. The Companions felt that too. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ did not tell them to panic.{/idea} He gave them a sentence of trust to hold.
old: Thinking about the Last Day should just make me scared.
new: The Prophet ﷺ answered that fear with trust: Allah is enough for us.
try: Say "HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal wakeel" three times today, slowly.

title: Whispering: we only stayed about ten days.
subtitle: How short life will feel
then: Ibn Abbas said they will be {idea}whispering among themselves{/idea}. They will say they stayed in the world only about ten days. The whole of life, looked back on, will seem like {trap}a little while{/trap}.
now: You keep saying "one day" I will start praying properly, fix things with my father, give more. {idea}Your whole life may feel like ten days when it is over.{/idea} "One day" is shorter than you think.
old: I have plenty of time to get serious later.
new: Life will feel like a few days when it ends. The time to act is now.
try: Do one thing today you have been postponing to "one day".

title: The wisest among them will say: only a single day.
subtitle: The clearest mind sees it even shorter
then: Ibn Kathir explains the one with the best mind will say {idea}one day{/idea}, because life's repeating nights, days and hours will feel like a single day. He cites another verse: {trap}you stayed but a little, if you had only known{/trap}.
now: Ask your grandmother how fast her life went. She will say, "Like a blink." {idea}The wiser you get, the shorter life looks.{/idea} So spend today like it matters, because it is a big piece of the whole.
old: Life is long, and today is just one of many.
new: The wisest see life as one day. Today is a big share of it.
try: Ask an elder today how fast life felt to them, and listen.

title: The mountains? My Lord will blow them away.
subtitle: Even the most solid things are temporary

row.title: only Allah
sub: and what is done for Him

then: People asked {idea}whether the mountains would remain on the Day of Resurrection{/idea}. The answer: My Lord will {trap}take them from their places, wipe them out and remove them completely{/trap}, scattered like dust.
now: The house you are paying off for 25 years. The company that has been around a century. The body you work so hard on at the gym. {idea}If mountains go, so will these.{/idea}
old: Some things in my life are solid and will always be there.
new: Even mountains will be blown away. Only what I do for Allah lasts.
try: Look at something that feels permanent today and say: this too will pass, Allah remains.

title: The whole earth left a flat, open plain.
subtitle: Nowhere left to hide
then: Ibn Kathir explains the earth becomes {idea}one expanse spread out{/idea}, level land. Some said it also means bare, with nothing growing. With the mountains gone, {trap}nothing is left standing between people and what is coming{/trap}.
now: You keep a few things hidden: the browser history, the side conversations, the version of you at work. {idea}One day the ground will be flat and open.{/idea} Living now as if nothing is hidden is a kind of freedom.
old: Some parts of my life can stay out of view forever.
new: One day everything will be in the open. I can start living openly now.
try: Clear out one hidden thing today that you would not want seen on that open plain.

title: Not a dip, not a rise anywhere.
subtitle: Every rank and level flattened
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and others said there will be {idea}no valley, no hill, no place low or high{/idea}. The earth that once had peaks and pits becomes completely even.
now: At work there is the corner office and the cleaner's cupboard. On the street, the big car and the bus stop. {idea}On that plain, nobody stands higher.{/idea} Treat people today the way they will be seen then.
old: Some people are simply above others.
new: One day the ground will be level. Only what I did will lift me.
try: Greet one person today you usually walk past, like the cleaner or the security guard.

title: Everyone follows the Caller, and voices fall silent.
subtitle: Obedience that comes too late
then: On that Day people will {idea}rush to the Caller wherever they are commanded{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes: {trap}if they had been like this in the worldly life, it would have helped them{/trap}, but there it does not. Ibn Abbas said nothing is heard but the steps of feet.
now: The adhan goes off on your phone and you hit snooze. One day you will run toward a call without hesitation. {idea}Answering now is what counts.{/idea}
old: I will respond to Allah's call when I am ready.
new: Everyone will answer that final call. Answering His call today is what helps me.
try: Respond to the very next adhan you hear within five minutes.

title: Intercession helps only by the Most Merciful's permission.
subtitle: No one speaks without His leave
then: Ibn Kathir explains no intercession helps {idea}except by Allah's permission{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ described falling in prostration under the Throne until told: {reward}intercede, and your intercession will be accepted{/reward}. Allah will bring out whoever has even a speck of faith.
now: You think, "My family is religious, my father was an imam, I will be fine." {idea}No one speaks for you without Allah's leave.{/idea} But His mercy reaches even a tiny seed of faith, so guard yours.
old: Being connected to good people will get me through.
new: All help on that Day comes by His permission. My own faith, however small, matters.
try: Ask Allah today to make you among those the Prophet ﷺ intercedes for.

title: He knows what is ahead and behind them.
subtitle: His knowledge surrounds ours
then: Ibn Kathir explains {idea}He encompasses all creation with His knowledge{/idea}, what has happened to them and what will happen. And people {trap}never encompass anything of His knowledge{/trap} except what He wills.
now: You lie awake trying to plan every outcome: the job, the move, the kids' future. {idea}You cannot see the whole.{/idea} He already knows what is ahead of you, and what is behind you that you have forgotten.
old: If I think hard enough, I can see how everything will turn out.
new: Only Allah sees what is before and behind me. I can plan and then trust.
try: Write down one worry about the future, then say: Allah knows what I do not.

title: All faces humbled; whoever carries wrongdoing fails.
subtitle: Before the Ever-Living, every wrong is settled
then: Ibn Abbas said all creatures will be {idea}humbled before the Ever-Living who does not die, the Sustainer who does not sleep{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says Allah will give every right to its owner, even {trap}the hornless ram against the horned one{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said wrongdoing will be darkness on that Day.
now: The money you borrowed and never returned. The sharp word to your younger brother. The colleague whose credit you took. {idea}Every wrong gets settled.{/idea} Settle it now, while it is easy.
old: Small wrongs I did long ago do not matter anymore.
new: Every wrong will be settled. Better to put it right while I still can.
try: Return one thing or apologise for one wrong today, however small.

title: Do good with faith, and fear no unfairness.
subtitle: Nothing added, nothing taken away
then: After the warning comes the comfort. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the believer who does good {reward}will not have his evils increased or his good deeds decreased{/reward}. Ibn Kathir explains Zulm is others' sins added to you; Hadm is your good being reduced. {idea}Neither will happen.{/idea}
now: You do your best at work and someone else gets the credit. You help family and nobody notices. Life is not always fair. {reward}Allah's judgement is.{/reward} Not one good deed will be shaved off.
old: My good deeds might get lost or not counted.
new: With faith, every good I do is fully kept. Nothing unfair will touch me.
try: Do one good deed today that you know no one will ever thank you for.
